title: Steve Prefontaine: Go Pre
description: A 1970s rebel who packed a historic track and challenged the system—five depths into myth and loss.

questions.question: Which 1970s American distance runner had Hayward Field crowds chanting "Go Pre"?
questions.explanation: Steve "Pre" Prefontaine turned Eugene's Hayward Field into a rock concert—front-running charisma that redefined track's fan culture.

questions.question: Prefontaine ran collegiately for which university in Eugene?
questions.explanation: He won seven NCAA titles for Oregon and lost only a handful of races at Hayward Field in his whole career—Bowerman's program became synonymous with Pre's swagger.

questions.question: Pre's coach at Oregon, Bill Bowerman, co-founded what shoe company with former runner Phil Knight?
questions.explanation: Bowerman's waffle-iron sole experiments and Knight's Blue Ribbon Sports became Nike—Pre wore the prototypes that sold the dream.

questions.question: Nike's early prototype runner Prefontaine died May 30, 1975, when his gold British sports car flipped—a what?
questions.explanation: He crashed his MGB roadster after a party in Eugene—24 years old, at the peak of his fight against amateurism's limits.

questions.question: After his MGB crash, Eugene still honors Pre each year at Hayward Field with the what Classic?
questions.explanation: The Prefontaine Classic (part of the Diamond League circuit) keeps his name on the same track where "Go Pre" once shook the stands.
